findings.title: Silence drawer never opens for rules rendered from promRule only (new alert list view)
findings.body: The silence drawer is rendered only when `rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)` is truthy, where `rule` is the optional RulerRuleDTO prop. In the new alert list view (FilterView → GrafanaRuleListItem → RuleActionsButtons), only `promRule` is passed and `rule` is undefined, so this condition is always false. However, the 'Silence notifications' menu item in AlertRuleMenu is shown based on the new promRule-based ability check (`useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` for AlertRuleAction.Silence), so a user with silencing permissions clicks 'Silence notifications', `setShowSilenceDrawer(true)` fires, and nothing renders — the action is a silent no-op. Either pass a Grafana prom-rule-compatible drawer or gate the menu item on the ruler rule being present. The new GrafanaGroupLoader test only asserts the menu item renders, not that the drawer opens, so this regression is untested.

findings.title: Delete and Pause menu items are unreachable in the new alert list view despite the new promRule ability checks
findings.body: AlertRuleMenu now ORs ruler-rule abilities with the new Grafana prom-rule abilities (`canDelete = (deleteSupported && deleteAllowed) || (grafanaDeleteSupported && grafanaDeleteAllowed)`, same for pause), which was added specifically so the list view can work without ruler data. But the render conditions were not updated: the Pause item requires `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule)` (line 123) and the Delete item requires `rulerRule` to be truthy (line 165, and `handleDelete` needs a RulerRuleDTO). Since the new list view (GrafanaRuleListItem → RuleActionsButtons) passes only `promRule` and no rulerRule, both `grafanaDeleteAbility` and `grafanaPauseAbility` results are dead code there: users with full permissions can no longer pause or delete Grafana-managed rules from the alert list, a regression from the previous GrafanaRuleLoader-based list which fetched ruler rules. The new GrafanaGroupLoader test that expects exactly 4 menu items (no Delete, no Pause) with all permissions granted confirms the actions are gone rather than this being intentional gating.

findings.title: GrafanaRuleListItem rendered without a key inside rules.map()
findings.body: In FilterViewResults, the switch over rule origin renders the new GrafanaRuleListItem without a `key` prop, while the 'datasource' and default branches both set `key={key}` on their elements. React will fall back to index-based reconciliation for these list items, producing a missing-key warning and causing component state (open dropdown menus, redirect-to-clone state, silence-drawer state held inside GrafanaRuleListItem/RuleActionsButtons) to be attached by position rather than by rule when the list changes, which can attach an open menu or pending action to the wrong rule. Pass `key={key}` like the other branches do.

findings.title: Federated rule group detection lost when useAllAlertRuleAbilities delegates to useAllRulerRuleAbilities
findings.body: The refactored `useAllAlertRuleAbilities(rule: CombinedRule)` now delegates to `useAllRulerRuleAbilities`, which hardcodes `const isFederated = false;` (line 245, with only a TODO to re-add support). The previous implementation computed `isFederated = isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group)`. Federated rule groups (Mimir/Metrics Enterprise cross-tenant rule federation) are read-only, and the federated flag fed into `immutableRule`, which disabled Update/Delete/Pause/Restore/DeletePermanently abilities. All existing consumers of `useAlertRuleAbility`/`useAlertRuleAbilities` with a CombinedRule (e.g. the RulesTable / RuleActionsButtons code paths) will now show Edit, Delete, and Pause actions for rules in federated groups, where previously they were hidden; attempting those actions against a federated group fails on the backend. The federated check must be preserved (e.g. by reading `source_tenants` from the group identifier or passing the CombinedRule's group through) before this delegation ships.

findings.title: Stale JSDoc and props comment reference the removed Ruler fetch
findings.body: The component JSDoc still says "Loads an evaluation group from Prometheus and Ruler endpoints" (line 25) and the `expectedRulesCount` prop comment (lines 16-21) still says "Ruler response might contain different number of rules", but this PR removed the `useGetGrafanaRulerGroupQuery` call and all ruler handling from GrafanaGroupLoader. The docs now describe behavior that no longer exists and will mislead maintainers.

findings.title: Comment and variable name reference removed ruler-rule preloading
findings.body: In `useGrafanaGroupsGenerator`, the comment at line 81 ("This is not mandatory to preload ruler rules, but it improves the UX / Because the user waits a bit longer for the initial load...") and the variable name `cacheAndRulerPreload` (line 84) describe the `alertRuleApi.util.prefetch('getGrafanaRulerGroup', ...)` call that this PR deleted. Only the prometheusApi cache upsert remains, so both the comment and the name are now wrong and should be updated.
